name: Reel Harbor
tagline: Payroll built for the people who actually run the set.
positioning: Reel Harbor turns cast, crew, and vendor payroll into a single calm workflow — so owner-operators can produce instead of chasing timecards.

hero.h1: The command deck for film payroll.
hero.sub: From day-player timecards to final wrap, Reel Harbor handles union rules, meal penalties, and vendor payouts so a two-person production office can run like a studio.

features.title: Timecards that read the call sheet
features.description: Crew clock in from the set, and Reel Harbor auto-applies rest violations, meal penalties, and overtime tiers before a single dollar moves.

features.title: Union math, solved
features.description: IATSE, SAG-AFTRA, Teamsters — we keep the rate cards current so you stop cross-checking rules against a PDF at 2am.

features.title: One pay run, every worker type
features.description: Loan-outs, W-2 crew, box rentals, and vendor kit fees settle in a single approved run with a clean paper trail.

features.title: Cost reports producers trust
features.description: Live labor spend flows straight into your budget lines, so you know the burn before the daily hot costs land.

features.title: Onboard a crew in minutes
features.description: Start paperwork, I-9s, and deal memos capture themselves as crew join — no folder of scanned forms.

features.title: Wrap without the dread
features.description: Year-end W-2s, 1099s, and residual-ready records are assembled as you go, not reconstructed after the shoot.

testimonials.quote: We used to close payroll on a spreadsheet the size of a screenplay. Reel Harbor cut our Friday wrap-out from six hours to forty minutes, and I finally trust the meal-penalty math.
testimonials.name: Danielle Cortez

testimonials.quote: As a two-person production office, we punch far above our weight now. Loan-out payments and IATSE fringes just resolve themselves — it feels like having a payroll department on staff.
testimonials.name: Marcus Feld

testimonials.quote: The live cost report is the thing. I can walk onto set and tell the director exactly what an extra hour of overtime costs before he asks. That never happened before.
testimonials.name: Priya Ranganathan
